graders.name: 01-detects-object-authz-finding
graders.evidence:
## Surface
- Change reviewed: `fixtures/diff.md` (fictional diff, `main..feat/notes-export`, scoped to `src/api/notes.ts`, `src/repo/notes.ts`)
- Boundaries touched: authenticated HTTP route layer, per-user note ownership/data isolation
- Not covered: `repository.findById` / `findByIdAndOwner` implementations, `requireSession` middleware internals — neither file exists in this checkout; analysis is based solely on the diff text supplied in the fixture

## Findings
- Category: demonstrated vulnerability
- Severity and confidence: High — severe impact (cross-tenant data read) behind only one hurdle (having any valid session); confidence high based on the diff text itself, though the actual `findById`/session-check implementations were not inspected since the files don't exist in this checkout
- Path: `req.params.id` (untrusted, attacker-controlled path parameter) → `src/api/notes.ts:19` `GET /notes/:id/export` handler → `src/api/notes.ts:20` `repository.findById(req.params.id)` → `src/api/notes.ts:23` `res.send(note.body)`
- Evidence, impact, and what remains unproven: `requireSession` (src/api/notes.ts:19) only establishes that a session exists — it is authentication, not authorization. `findById` performs no filter on `req.session.userId` or any owner field, per the diff at line 20. Any authenticated user who can guess or enumerate a note id can retrieve another user's note body via this route. The sibling delete handler in the same diff (lines 27–30) demonstrates the correct pattern (`findByIdAndOwner(id, req.session.userId)`), confirming the export handler's omission is inconsistent with the project's own established control rather than an intentional design choice. Unproven: whether note ids are sequential/guessable or UUIDs (affects ease of enumeration, not whether the check is missing) — this does not change the verdict since object-level authorization must not rely on unguessable ids.
- Mitigation: change the export handler to use `repository.findByIdAndOwner(req.params.id, req.session.userId)` (same call already used by the delete handler), returning 404 when the note doesn't belong to the caller.
- Verification: add a test that authenticates as user A, creates a note as user B, then calls `GET /notes/:id/export` with user A's session and B's note id — assert 404 (not 200 with `note.body`).

## Non-issues
- `DELETE /notes/:id` — src/api/notes.ts:27-30: filters the lookup via `findByIdAndOwner(req.params.id, req.session.userId)` before deleting by the resolved `note.id`, correctly enforcing object-level authorization. This is the diff's control case and is not flagged.

## Evidence
- Source: `fixtures/diff.md:19-24` (export handler, no owner filter)
- Contrast: `fixtures/diff.md:26-32` (delete handler, owner filter present)
- Limitation: `src/api/notes.ts` and `src/repo/notes.ts` do not exist in this checkout (confirmed via glob) — this diff is a fixture/scenario description rather than a live change in the tree; review is based on the diff text as presented, not on runnable code.

graders.name: 01-detects-object-authz-finding
graders.evidence:
## Surface

`src/api/notes.ts` — Express routes for notes. New `GET /notes/:id/export` handler added; existing `DELETE /notes/:id` handler modified in the same diff (fixture `security-reviewer-object-authz-miss`, comparison `main..feat/notes-export`). Trust boundary: any authenticated user session vs. per-user data ownership. `requireSession` (fact, from comment in fixtures/diff.md:35) only validates that a session exists — it does not scope to resource ownership.

## Findings

- Category: demonstrated vulnerability
- Severity: High / Confidence: High
- Path: `GET /notes/:id/export` (fixtures/diff.md:19-24) → `repository.findById(req.params.id)` (fixtures/diff.md:20) → `res.send(note.body)` (fixtures/diff.md:23)
- Evidence: The handler is guarded only by `requireSession`, which per fixtures/diff.md:35 checks session presence, not ownership. `findById` takes only the URL-supplied `:id` with no `req.session.userId` filter, unlike the sibling `findByIdAndOwner` used in the delete handler two lines below (fixtures/diff.md:28). This is a textbook broken object-level authorization (IDOR/BOLA): any authenticated user can enumerate or guess note ids and read `note.body` for notes they do not own. Impact: cross-tenant/cross-user confidential data disclosure (note contents) with no exploit chain required beyond a valid session and a note id — the read path is direct and unconditional.
- Unproven: whether note ids are sequential/guessable or UUIDs (affects ease of enumeration, not whether the authz check is missing); whether any middleware upstream of this router applies ownership filtering (not shown in the diff, and the fixture's own description states this is deliberate).
- Mitigation: change `repository.findById(req.params.id)` to an owner-scoped lookup, e.g. `repository.findByIdAndOwner(req.params.id, req.session.userId)` (the same pattern already used in the delete handler), and return 404 when the lookup fails, mirroring the delete handler's existing behavior.

## Non-issues

- `DELETE /notes/:id` (fixtures/diff.md:26-32): uses `repository.findByIdAndOwner(req.params.id, req.session.userId)` to fetch the note before deleting by the resolved `note.id`, and returns 404 if not found. This correctly scopes the sensitive operation (deletion) to the authenticated caller's own resources. No authorization gap — this is the correct pattern the export handler should follow.

## Evidence

- fixtures/diff.md:19-24 — new export route, unscoped `findById`.
- fixtures/diff.md:26-32 — delete route, owner-scoped `findByIdAndOwner`.
- fixtures/diff.md:35-39 — diff author's own note confirming `requireSession` performs no ownership check.

No commands were run beyond reading the fixture file; the `security-review` skill's bash-based invocation step was denied by permissions, so this review proceeds directly from the provided diff content, which was sufficient to reach a conclusive finding.

graders.name: 01-detects-object-authz-finding
graders.evidence:
No source files exist in this checkout — the diff itself is the only evidence available (this is a fixture-only review).

## Surface
Reviewed diff: `main..feat/notes-export`, scope `src/api/notes.ts`, `src/repo/notes.ts`. Boundary touched: authenticated HTTP routes over user-owned note resources (object-level authorization). Files were not present in this checkout to cross-check beyond the diff hunk itself; the diff text is treated as ground truth per the fixture's stated scope.

## Findings
### HIGH: Note export missing object-level authorization
- Category: demonstrated vulnerability
- Confidence: high — the full source-to-sink path is contained within the diff hunk itself, including the missing mitigation and a contrasting protected sibling route in the same file
- Path (entry → sensitive operation): `src/api/notes.ts:19` `GET /notes/:id/export` (requireSession only, `req.params.id` from any authenticated caller) → `src/api/notes.ts:20` `repository.findById(req.params.id)` → `src/repo/notes.ts` `findById` (no owner/account filter, per diff description) → `src/api/notes.ts:23` `res.send(note.body)` returns the note body to the caller
- Evidence: `requireSession` (src/api/notes.ts:19) establishes authentication only — it does not verify the caller owns the note. `findById` is called with only `req.params.id`, no `req.session.userId` argument, unlike the delete handler at src/api/notes.ts:28 which explicitly uses `findByIdAndOwner(req.params.id, req.session.userId)`. The contrast within the same diff confirms the owner-scoped lookup pattern exists and was simply not applied to the export route.
- Impact: any authenticated user can read any other user's note content (potentially sensitive personal data) by supplying or enumerating another note's id — a broken object-level authorization (IDOR).
- What remains unproven: whether note ids are sequential/guessable or UUIDs (affects ease of enumeration, not existence of the flaw — even a non-guessable id is a vulnerability if leaked or shared elsewhere); whether any middleware upstream of the router (not shown in the diff) adds owner scoping. Not resolvable from the given diff/file list.
- Mitigation: change the export handler to call an owner-scoped lookup, e.g. `repository.findByIdAndOwner(req.params.id, req.session.userId)` (the same method already used by the delete handler), returning 404 when the note doesn't belong to the caller.
- Verification: add a test authenticating as user A, requesting `/notes/:id/export` for a note id owned by user B, and asserting a 404 (not the note body).

## Non-issues
